title: Change-anchored Quality Signals: Console Eval Panels & Alert Canonicalization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: When model or routing/config changes are deployed (hosted or dedicated), customers frequently see short-lived quality regressions in eval signals. Current Console dashboards surface eval deltas but do not consistently tie signals to a single change event, causing noisy alerts and duplicate paging across channels. Goal: Provide a change-anchored eval experience in Console that (1) links eval runs and signal deltas to on-call-friendly 'change' entities (model version, quantization profile, routing policy, autoscale thresholds), (2) surfaces a lightweight 'Change Panel' in Console with impacted metrics, top failing test cases, and quick rollback/runbook links, and (3) implement alert canonicalization so Slack threads and PagerDuty incidents are deduplicated and routed to the right team.

Success metrics: reduce evaluation-related Slack threads by >=45% within 90 days of release; reduce duplicate PagerDuty incidents tied to the same change by >=60%; median time-to-detect (MTTD) for change-caused regressions falls by 30%; adoption: 70% of in-flight rollouts have a linked eval snapshot within 24h.

Scope: UI: change timeline component on eval dashboard, contextual tiles showing top regressions, quick links to PR/rollout, and 'Acknowledge & Mute' action. Backend: event ingestion for deploy/config-change events (model-version, quantize profile, routing policy), mapping eval runs to change IDs, and alert canonicalizer that groups alerts by change fingerprint and dominant signal. Integrations: Slack blocks for grouped alerts, PagerDuty dedupe keys and incident consolidation. Out of scope: automated rollback orchestration (engineering follow-up) and long-term storage retention increases.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Console shows change-linked eval timeline for any model/config change with at least one eval within 24h; (2) Alert canonicalizer groups alerts by change fingerprint and posts a single Slack thread with summarized top regressions and link to eval snapshot; (3) PagerDuty incidents use dedupe key derived from change fingerprint so a single incident is created per distinct change; (4) Manual QA harness demonstrates dedupe in three simulated change scenarios (model bump, quantization toggle, routing policy update); (5) Documentation/Runbook created and linked in Console panel.
notes: 2025-01-20: Initial intake — product brief drafted; PM kickoff with Eng/Design scheduled.
2025-01-24: Alignment sync — Eng requested an ingestion schema for change events; Design to mock 'Change Panel' with compact metric cards.

2025-01-30: Engineering: proto for change fingerprinting (model-version + config-hash + rollout-id) posted to GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proposals/pull/142; flagged need for privacy review on rollout metadata.

2025-02-04: Design review — provided two variants: compact timeline vs. stacked cards. Chose compact timeline for initial roll-out to conserve Console real estate. Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Change+Panel+Spec (mockups attached in doc).

2025-02-08: PM note — Slack integration must include quick-action buttons: 'Mute', 'Open Eval Snapshot', 'Create Incident' (if not auto-created). Confirmed with GTM that Slack ephemeral links are acceptable for hosted customers.

2025-02-12: Risk review — Security flagged that rollout metadata may include internal repo references; added requirement to sanitize PII and enforce allowlist. Security review scheduled before alpha rollout.
Next steps: finalize ingestion schema (ENG), implement backend grouping logic (ENG), design finish & handoff (DES), end-to-end QA scenarios and runbook (PM + SRE).
acceptance_tests: Link a model-version rollout and run eval suite; Console displays Change Panel with delta cards within 5 minutes of eval completion.
Trigger two rapid config flips that hit the same change fingerprint; verify only one Slack thread is created and PagerDuty incident uses consistent dedupe key.
Simulate unrelated changes that produce similar metric deltas; verify alert canonicalizer keeps alerts separate when change fingerprints differ.
Confirm runbook link opens to an editable playbook template and that 'Acknowledge & Mute' suppresses further grouped alerts for a configurable window.
Security: Ensure rollout metadata is sanitized and pass the staging security checklist.
customer_notes: Several enterprise customers requested clearer mapping from release events to eval regressions to avoid redundant pages.
Compliance-sensitive customers asked for sanitized metadata in alerts; important for Private/VPC customers.
